name: KYONO JUICE（キョウノ ジュース） (Kyono Juice)

claims.text: Listed on Japan VegeMap as a fully vegan (すべてヴィーガン) cold-pressed juice and smoothie shop, so the kitchen handles essentially no animal products, greatly reducing the risk of animal cross-contact.
No published allergen handling info; the VegeMap listing explicitly advises confirming allergen and ingredient details directly with the shop.
Menu is centered on raw cold-pressed fruit-and-vegetable juices, smoothies and cold-pressed sodas — naturally plant-based and, for the juices, inherently free of wheat/gluten.

Wheat is central to the menu: fresh namafu (wheat gluten) and house-made natural-yeast bread are signature ingredients, so gluten is present throughout the kitchen and cross-contact with wheat should be assumed.
Soy sauce is used in the cooking but there is no confirmation it is wheat-free; standard Japanese shoyu contains wheat, so assume gluten unless confirmed directly with the restaurant.
The kitchen is 100% vegan — no dairy, eggs, fish, meat or honey are used anywhere — so the risk of animal-product cross-contact is essentially eliminated.
Vegewel and HappyCow both list the restaurant as fully plant-based / 100% vegan with all dishes safe for vegans.

The owner states they normally do not accommodate food allergies, but has made exceptions when no other guests are present; the owner also has food allergies and understands the difficulties. Discuss any needs at the time of (mandatory) reservation.
English-speaking staff and an English menu are available, which makes communicating dietary questions easier.
Entirely plant-based kitchen, so vegan diners can order anything on the course menu without worrying about hidden animal products, dashi or honey.
Intimate, low-volume operation where dishes are prepared with care; reviewers praise the creativity, presentation and the owner's attentive hospitality.

name: 京のカレーうどん 味味香 祇園店 (Mimikou (Kyo no Curry Udon Mimikou, Gion)

claims.text: Primarily a wheat-udon shop; udon and ramen noodles are wheat, and battered tempura shares the kitchen, so high gluten cross-contact for any non-noodle order.
The broth/sauce is seasoned with soy sauce (regular Japanese shoyu, typically wheat-based); no wheat-free tamari is mentioned.

A May 2025 diner reported staff disclosed that everything is fried in the same oil (tofu, meat and fish), so fried toppings like tempura and soy meat carry animal cross-contact and are not strictly vegan.
It is an omnivore restaurant serving meat and fish dishes alongside the vegetarian menu, so shared cookware/oil should be assumed.
Staff openly disclosed the shared-oil situation when a vegan customer asked, indicating they will answer ingredient/preparation questions if you ask.
There is a separate English vegetarian/vegan menu, and the vegetarian udon broth is explicitly made without fish stock, using a kombu/seaweed base instead of bonito dashi.
Vegan can be ordered by declining the optional egg add-on; vegan curry udon, vegan dashi ramen and vegetable curry rice are available with soy-meat and vegetable toppings.
The signature monpan is a wheat flatbread and the kitchen also makes yakisoba, noodles, pasta and Korean pancakes, so wheat is handled throughout; no gluten-free preparation protocols are documented.
No information found on whether the soy sauce or sauces used are wheat-free; assume standard (wheat-containing) soy sauce unless confirmed.
Meat dishes are served from the same home kitchen as the vegan options, so some cross-contact is possible; ask for dishes to be made vegan.

A reviewer reported the owner understood a vegan order and took allergies into account when handed an explanation written in Japanese — individual accommodation appears possible if you communicate clearly.
Vegan items are clearly marked on the menu and staff will veganize many dishes on request, so plant-based diners have genuine, varied choices.
Small, attentive owner-run kitchen where food is prepared to order, which makes custom dietary requests easier to handle.

name: ナチュラルフード ビレッジ (Natural Food Village)

claims.text: No gluten-free program advertised; menu features wheat-based proteins (soy meat / soy cutlet) and battered/fried items (tempeh tempura) and noodles, so shared frying oil and surfaces likely carry gluten.
No confirmation that wheat-free (tamari) soy sauce is used; assume standard wheat-containing soy sauce in seasonings and sauces unless staff confirm otherwise.
Entirely plant-based kitchen with no meat, fish, dairy or eggs used, so risk of animal-product cross-contact is inherently very low.
Fully vegan since 2001 — every dish is plant-based, making it a safe and easy choice for vegan and vegetarian diners.
Uses organic, pesticide-free vegetables, carefully selected seasonings and Kitashirakawa groundwater, with an English menu and friendly owner.

name: おめんNIPPON 四条先斗町店 (Omen NIPPON Shijo Pontocho)

claims.text: This is a wheat-udon kitchen; the noodles, tempura batter and standard tare all contain wheat, so there is heavy gluten presence throughout. No gluten-free preparation or separate handling was described — not suitable for celiac diners.
No wheat-free soy sauce or tamari was mentioned; the dipping sauce/seasonings should be assumed to contain wheat-based soy sauce.

The vegan set uses a separately prepared vegan dashi and egg-free tempura, but the kitchen also handles meat and seafood (e.g., prawn tempura). One reviewer reported being mistakenly served the non-vegan version with prawns, so confirm your order.

Vegan/vegetarian orders are accommodated on request with a distinct broth and sides, and an English menu is available, but plant-based is not the default and at least one order mix-up has been reported — communicate your needs clearly.
A dedicated vegan/vegetarian set is available with a fish-free (kelp/vegetable) dashi, fresh and pickled seasonal vegetables, ground sesame and egg-free vegetable tempura.
English menu and staff experienced with international visitors make it easy to request the vegan option.
Bread and pasta are core to the menu (shiitake/negi breads, maitake pasta), so wheat and gluten are heavily present in the kitchen; no gluten-free protocol is documented.

This is an omnivore kitchen whose standard course includes fish, octopus, duck and house-made bacon, so animal ingredients are handled alongside the vegan course; the vegan menu is prepared to order rather than in a separate animal-free kitchen.

The restaurant asks guests to inform them of all allergies and dislikes in advance and states it cannot accommodate requests made after arrival — so any dietary needs must be arranged at the time of reservation.
The kitchen offers a true 100% vegan course and defines vegan strictly as no meat, fish, shellfish, dairy, eggs or honey, indicating clear understanding of plant-based requirements.
One of the few high-end Kyoto restaurants offering a genuine full vegan multi-course menu built around seasonal Kyoto vegetables, herbs and edible flowers.
Because the vegan course is reserved and prepared individually in advance, the chef can plan a fully animal-free plate rather than improvising on arrival.

name: ロンハーマンカフェ 京都店 (Ron Herman Cafe Kyoto)

claims.text: No gluten-free menu or dedicated GF preparation was documented; as a general cafe serving cakes and baked goods, wheat cross-contact is likely. Gluten-sensitive guests should confirm each dish with staff.

This is an omnivore kitchen that also serves meat and dairy dishes, so plant-based items are not prepared in an animal-free environment; shared equipment cross-contact is possible. Cooked-to-order preparation does reduce some shared-batch risk.
Staff explicitly ask guests to tell them about food allergies and disliked ingredients, and because dishes are cooked to order they say they can accommodate requests as much as possible.
Several clearly labeled vegan dishes are offered with no animal-derived ingredients, including a vegetable rice bowl, avocado cake and oat-milk drinks.
The cafe emphasizes pesticide-free organic vegetables grown with contract farmers from the soil up.
Cook-to-order kitchen with a stated willingness to adjust dishes for allergies and dietary needs.
